epic.title: Energy - Supplier integration: New supplier via API
epic.summary: Add a new energy supplier to the peasy.be energy comparison. Tariffs sync daily via the supplier API and switches are ordered through the same API.
epic.problem: Users can only compare and switch to current partners. Each new supplier today means manual tariff updates and manual order hand-over.
goals: More offers for households in all three regions
Switch without re-entering data at the supplier
Reusable API integration for the next supplier
metrics: Completed switches to the new supplier / month
dependencies: PEASY-XXX Supplier screen: supplier must exist in the Energy Engine
PEASY-XXX Electricity product specifications (New Engine Admin)
Grid and tax tariffs (Nettarieven, Heffingen) for the all-in yearly price
Signed partner agreement + API docs and sandbox from the supplier
Legal: consent text, privacy notice, data agreement with the supplier

details.title: Non-functional
table: API credentials in secrets store; TLS only; no personal data in logs
Personal data sent only to perform the requested switch; consent logged with timestamp
WCAG 2.2 AA; errors in text, not colour only
Results load time unchanged; tariffs read from Peasy store
Sync and order metrics, alerts on failure rate, runbook for Ops
Feature flag per supplier = kill switch without deploy

notes: Ranking stays neutral: total yearly cost incl. VAT and grid costs.
Ranking and remuneration are disclosed on the results page (consumer law, CREG comparison rules: Legal to confirm).
Results read tariffs from Peasy's store, never live from the API.

tickets.title: Energy - Supplier integration: Import tariffs daily
tickets.description: Import the supplier's electricity and gas tariffs from its API every night, with their validity period.

ac.title: Valid tariffs are stored
ac.given: the nightly sync runs at [02:00 CET]
then: tariffs are stored per region and grid operator
each tariff keeps its valid-from and valid-to date

ac.title: Re-import does not duplicate
ac.given: a tariff already exists
ac.when: the same tariff is imported again
ac.then: it is updated, not duplicated

ac.title: Invalid records are rejected
ac.given: a record misses a required field
then: the error is logged for Ops

ac.title: API errors keep previous tariffs
ac.given: the API times out or errors
ac.then: it retries [3] times, then keeps the last valid tariffs

notes: Required fields: €/kWh, fixed fee, contract length, green %, region, valid-from.
API contract, rate limit and pagination: see Backend Technical Document.

tickets.title: Energy - Supplier integration: Map products to the comparison model
tickets.description: Map supplier products to Peasy's energy model so they compare like-for-like with other suppliers.

ac.title: Mapped products are comparable
ac.given: a supplier product is imported
ac.then: every field in the mapping table is filled or the product is rejected

ac.title: Unsupported fields are kept, not shown
ac.given: the supplier sends an unknown field
ac.then: it is stored as a provider extra and not displayed

ac.title: No tariff for grid operator
ac.given: a product has no tariff for the user's grid operator
ac.then: the product is not shown

notes: Supplier prices are stored excl. VAT; VAT, grid and tax tariffs are added by the Energy Engine.

tickets.title: Energy - Supplier integration: Show supplier in results
tickets.description: Show the new supplier in energy results, ranked like every other supplier.

ac.title: Supplier is ranked neutrally
ac.given: the user completes the energy flow
ac.then: the supplier is ranked by total yearly cost
and: equal prices keep the existing tie-break rule

ac.title: Result card shows key data
ac.given: the supplier's result card
then: € per month and € per year incl. VAT and grid costs

ac.title: Existing filters apply
ac.given: the user filters on 100% green
ac.then: the existing green filter rules apply

ac.title: Current supplier is handled
ac.given: the user's current supplier is the new supplier
ac.then: the existing current-supplier handling applies

ac.title: Ranking is explained
ac.given: the results page
ac.then: the ranking and remuneration note is visible

copy: € XX per maand · € XX per jaar, incl. btw en netkosten
We rangschikken op totale jaarprijs. Hoe we vergelijken en verdienen: zo werkt Peasy.
notes: Logo: supplier delivers SVG + usage rights.

tickets.title: Energy - Supplier integration: Hide supplier on stale tariffs
tickets.description: Hide the supplier when its tariffs are outdated so we never show or sell wrong prices.

ac.title: Stale supplier is hidden
ac.given: the last sync is older than [48 h]
ac.then: the supplier is hidden from results and the switch flow

ac.title: User mid-flow is redirected
ac.given: the user is on the review screen
then: the user returns to refreshed results with a message

ac.title: Ops is alerted
ac.given: the supplier is hidden
ac.then: Ops gets an alert in [channel] with reason and last sync time

ac.title: Supplier returns automatically
ac.given: a valid sync completes
ac.then: the supplier is shown again

copy: Deze prijs is niet meer beschikbaar. Bekijk de bijgewerkte resultaten.

tickets.title: Energy - Supplier integration: Review and validate switch details
tickets.description: Let the user check contract, address and EAN codes and give consent before the order is sent.

ac.title: Review screen shows the deal
ac.given: the user clicks Overstappen
then: product, contract length, € per month and per year
start date at least [35] days ahead

ac.title: Validation blocks invalid input
ac.given: a required field is empty or an EAN is invalid
then: a message shows below the field

ac.title: Consent is required
ac.given: consent is not ticked
ac.then: the consent message shows and nothing is sent

copy: Vul een geldige EAN-code in (18 cijfers, begint met 54).
notes: EAN: 18 digits, starts with 54; check-digit rule: Tech to confirm.
Privacy: address and EAN are personal data, never logged.

tickets.title: Energy - Supplier integration: Submit the switch order via API
tickets.description: Send the confirmed switch to the supplier API exactly once, at the price the user saw.

ac.title: Order is sent
ac.given: the user confirms with valid data and consent
ac.then: the order is sent to the supplier API

ac.title: Price is re-checked
ac.given: the tariff changed since results loaded
then: the user sees the new price and confirms again

ac.title: Order is sent once
ac.given: an order is in progress
ac.when: the user clicks again or refreshes
ac.then: no second order is sent (idempotency key per quote)

ac.title: No automatic retry
ac.given: the API does not answer within [10 s]
ac.then: the order is not resent and goes to expert fallback

notes: Payload: name, address, EAN codes, start date, contact. Privacy: send only these fields.
Idempotency key = quote ID + user ID.

tickets.title: Energy - Supplier integration: Expert fallback on failed order
tickets.description: When the API rejects or times out, save the request and let a Peasy expert finish the switch.

ac.title: Failure is handled
ac.given: the API rejects or times out
then: a callback task is created for Ops

ac.title: Callback task has context
ac.given: a callback task is created
ac.then: it shows the user, chosen product, error and time

copy: We konden je aanvraag nog niet doorsturen. Geen zorgen: je gegevens zijn bewaard. Een Peasy-expert belt je binnen [SLA].

tickets.title: Energy - Supplier integration: Track order status and notify
tickets.description: Store each order's status, email the customer on changes and report switches and failures.

ac.title: Status is stored
ac.given: an order is sent
ac.then: status is saved as sent, accepted, rejected or failed with timestamp

ac.title: Customer is emailed
ac.given: the status changes to accepted or rejected
ac.then: the customer gets the matching email

ac.title: Events are tracked
ac.given: an order changes status
ac.then: it is sent to [analytics tool] with supplier_id, order_id, status

notes: Events: supplier_result_shown, switch_order_sent, switch_order_accepted, switch_order_failed, supplier_hidden_stale.
Status via callback or polling: Tech to confirm.
Privacy: emails use existing customer templates; no EAN in email body.

tickets.title: Energy - Supplier integration: Design result, review and confirmation screens
tickets.description: Design the result card, review and confirmation screens, including stale, validation and API-failure states. Needed before TBD-103 and TBD-105.

questions: Which supplier, and is the contract signed?
API: order status callbacks, SLA, rate limit, sandbox?
Stale threshold, retry count, alert channel?
Callback SLA and Ops capacity for failed orders?
Consent text, privacy notice, data agreement, ranking disclosure?
Is EN copy needed on peasy.be, or NL/FR only?
assumptions: API covers all regions and grid operators, electricity and gas.
API accepts orders with EAN, address, start date and returns a reference.
Old-contract cancellation works as for current suppliers.
risks: Price re-check at submit, stale hiding
rollout: Phase 0: sandbox + contract tests, internal QA
Phase 1: flag on for 10% of Flanders traffic; go/no-go on API success ≥ [X]%
Option: ship tariffs + expert-handled switch first, API order second (lower risk)
Before launch: support FAQ, Ops runbook, internal comms
dod: All ACs pass in QA on staging
Contract tests against supplier sandbox green
NL and FR copy live; Legal sign-off on consent and ranking text
Alerts and dashboard live; runbook shared with Ops
